name: 40269-chatdecode-1.7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1; the draft's tensor-parallel size must equal the target's.
architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM, bf16, 28 layers, 16 query / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, vocab 151936, tied embeddings; read off the checkpoints' own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=4, bounded at 320 requests / 1800 s safety, warmup 25% by completion; `max-num-seqs: 16` in vllm-config.yaml is a hard ceiling on concurrency.
workload: guidellm `json_file`, single turn: `configs/data/mtbench-turn1-qwen3.jsonl`, the 80 MT-Bench first turns, cycled to the 320-request bound. Prompts are the data's (mean 68 raw tokens, max 356; the chat template adds 8 to every row). Output is fixed at 256 tokens per request (max_tokens=256 with ignore_eos), sampled at temperature 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / top_k 0, declared both client-side in scenario.json and server-side by `generation-config: vllm`.
purpose: A compact chat assistant answering single-turn questions with 256-token replies for four concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B

# HAZARD: this value must stay on ONE line of JSON. The config reader is a flat line reader that
# skips indented lines, so a block mapping is dropped whole and the engine starts with NO
# speculative decoding at all, silently, at rc 0.
speculative-config: {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}

tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
max-num-seqs: 16
generation-config: vllm
enable-prefix-caching: false
dtype: bfloat16
enforce-eager: false
seed: 40269
